author: Peach Tree Times
title: AgGeorgia Farm Credit awards $5,000 grant to Pulaski County Fire Department for wildfire protection
text:
AgGeorgia Farm Credit announced on June 10 that it awarded a $5,000 grant to the Pulaski County Fire Department through its Community Mission Fund. The funding has enabled the department to fully equip two brush trucks with firefighting tools, enhancing wildfire response capabilities in central Georgia’s rural and agricultural areas.
Pulaski County is an important center for timber, livestock, and row-crop production in Georgia. The fire department serves more than 10,000 residents across 250 square miles. For this small combination fire agency, maintaining specialized equipment is essential to protect local farm families’ livelihoods.
The grant addressed what AgGeorgia described as a critical need for rapid-response gear. The funds were used by the department to outfit their brush trucks with a comprehensive suite of tools designed specifically for rural firefighting challenges.
“In a predominantly agricultural community like Hawkinsville, even a small fire can quickly threaten crops, equipment, and homes,” said Hawkinsville City Commissioner Ken Clark. “With limited financial resources and a rising call volume, this AgGeorgia funding directly improves our readiness to protect the assets that drive our local economy.”
“Our mission at AgGeorgia extends beyond providing credit; it’s about investing in the safety and future of the communities where our member-borrowers live and work,” said AgGeorgia’s Chief Marketing Officer Corey Cottle.
AgGeorgia Farm Credit supports local organizations through its Community Mission Fund by backing initiatives such as agricultural education programs, veteran services, emergency response projects, and environmental education efforts. The organization maintains 15 branches throughout Georgia and employs over 130 staff members who serve more than 5,000 member-borrowers statewide, according to the official website. AgGeorgia is owned by its member-borrowers and affiliates with the nationwide Farm Credit System. It aims to enhance farmers’ well-being through financial aid initiatives and offers a dividend program allowing members to share in cooperative profits.
